title: Generate and commit a hash-pinned lockfile for onfinance-db-model-master
description: In applications/db-models/repos/onfinance-db-model-master (OnFinance/onfinance_db_model_master, default branch master), setup.py line 19 declares install_requires=["mongoengine==0.24.1"] and no lockfile exists anywhere in the repo. From the repo root in a clean Python 3 virtualenv with pip-tools installed, run `python -m piptools compile --generate-hashes --index-url https://pypi.org/simple --output-file requirements.txt setup.py`. That registry is the only one allowed for Python by sdlc/policy.json dependencyPolicy.allowedRegistries. Commit the resulting requirements.txt, including the pip-tools header naming the command, with every direct and transitive dependency (mongoengine and pymongo and their dependencies) pinned to an exact version and sha256 hashes. Do not change setup.py install_requires. Add one line to the repo README stating that dependency changes must regenerate requirements.txt with the same command. Merge through a PR on protected master with at least one non-author approval. This is a dev-only library with no runtime, so no deployment window applies.
acceptanceCriteria: `git -C applications/db-models/repos/onfinance-db-model-master show master:requirements.txt` exists and contains `mongoengine==0.24.1` and a `pymongo==<exact version>` line, and every pinned package line is followed by at least one `--hash=sha256:` entry
In a fresh virtualenv, `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements.txt` exits 0
Re-running the same pip-tools compile command on master leaves `git status --porcelain requirements.txt` empty (no drift)
A re-run of probe-sdlc for db-models/onfinance-db-model-master no longer yields rule ssdf-pw-4-1-missing-lockfile (fingerprint 96f1cf43c2e58353fcaf38eca2a3f6d8dee5606394f80246184c72c634580c23)

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-sdlc scoped to db-models repo onfinance-db-model-master at the new master commit. Expected: the lockfile check finds requirements.txt with hashes, the SARIF export has no ssdf-pw-4-1-missing-lockfile result on setup.py, and the finding can be resolved under the absence rule.

rootCause.description: db-models was packaged with a bare setuptools setup.py and has no CI (ciSystem none), so dependencyPolicy.lockfilesRequired was never applied. Nothing in the repo's workflow ever generated a lockfile or checked that one exists.
